05 / Before you call it a good deal

What a buyer should look for.

01

Check the area denominator

Ask for net internal area and common-area shares separately. A cheap €/m² on total marketed area can be expensive on usable space. House and land areas are especially hard to compare.

02

Separate today's home from a promise

Ask for the documented construction and occupancy status, handover date and exact specification. A future completion year or “Акт 16” in an advertisement is a claim to verify, not proof of readiness.

03

Compare the total purchase

Get written prices for mandatory parking, VAT treatment, finishing, maintenance and agency charges. Compare properties with the same inclusions before negotiating from these benchmarks.

04

Visit the street, not just the apartment

Test the commute at your actual travel time. Inspect access, drainage, utility connections, traffic noise, parking and nearby construction. For a hillside home, check slope and water management with an appropriate specialist.

05

Match the legal identity

Compare the advertised area and address with the property's cadastral identifier and documents. The cadastral records contain property boundaries, areas and identifying details. Official cadastral guidance ↗

06

Verify rights and encumbrances

Have a qualified professional review ownership and the relevant registry documents. A property certificate reports registered rights and encumbrances at the time it is issued. Registry Agency guidance ↗

The evidence behind the report

Know what the sample can—and cannot—say.

Read the methodology & limitations

Only SALE records from the 22 October collection are included. The eight neighbourhoods are matched from reported location text. Mixed villa zones and industrial zones are excluded; Manastirski Livadi east/west are combined. No street coordinates were available. This is an editorial geographic selection, not a measured radius.

Likely duplicate groups require equal neighbourhood, normalised category, asking price, area, floor and the first 240 alphanumeric characters of a description longer than 240 characters. The rule may merge similar units in one development and miss the same home advertised differently. Counts are tentative groups, not unique property inventory. All grouped source links remain available.

Room types are inferred from listing titles; legacy English bedroom fields were not trusted. Uncertain room counts stay Unclassified. Benchmarks use positive EUR asking prices ≥ €10,000, areas 15–3,000 m² and €100–15,000/m². These are transparent screening bounds, not truth checks. Other currencies and screened-out records remain in the listing table, without benchmark labels. No currency conversion is applied.

Quantiles use linear interpolation between sorted observations. Neighbourhood bands and medians are withheld below n=8. A “lower-quartile” asking price means at or below the 25th percentile of the relevant peer sample. It is not an appraisal, promised discount, recommended bid, or proof of good value. No transaction prices, independent property inspections, exact building identities or availability checks were obtained.

The crawl stopped with partial/failure status for every source. Broad search caps, parsing failures and ordering effects can bias neighbourhood and category coverage. Rentals are excluded. Source ads may overlap and may contain stale or erroneous details. Capture time is not the date an ad was first listed. The report does not update itself as source websites change.
